---
title: "Composite Snapshots and Recursive Expansion"
subtitle: "How does a custom Python factory become one portable finite physical graph?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `STABILIZED` Full V1 implementation; originally accepted in the
`1.0.0.dev4` Lessons 6–8 scope. The
[Component Authoring Contract](../component-authoring.qmd#composite-snapshot-boundary)
owns the public `CompositePlan` and `ComponentInstance` behavior; this page
fixes the maintainer mechanism that realizes it.

## Freeze factories in Python, not during a solve

A custom Library factory is ordinary Python authoring code. It may construct a
`CompositePlan`, declare public parameters and baselines, add components, net
child pins, attach child endpoints to the eventual Plan ground, expose selected
pins or coordinates, and call `build()`. `build()` validates and freezes that
complete declaration into one immutable `ComponentInstance` before the outer
`CircuitPlan` receives it.

The sealed Plan stores the built snapshot, not a callable factory, Python
object graph, import name to resolve later, callback, expression AST, or
Notebook execution state. A factory runs neither during `CircuitRun` sealing
nor in Julia. An exception, a missing public map, an incomplete node, or a
cycle leaves no partial `ComponentInstance` to add to a Plan. Factory source
provenance remains required at creation time under
[Catalog and Runtime Identity](catalog-and-runtime-identity.qmd#prove-a-factory-when-it-creates-a-component).

This makes the boundary explicit:

```text
Python factory -> built immutable snapshot -> CircuitPlan hash -> Julia expansion
```

The first arrow is authoring. The remaining arrows consume data only.

## Represent every nested child with path segments

Every component occurrence has a `component_path`: an array of nonempty child
ID segments from its outer Plan component to that occurrence. For example, a
Plan component named `filter` containing `readout` containing `section_03` has
the path `["filter", "readout", "section_03"]`. Paths are arrays, never
slash-joined strings, so child IDs cannot create ambiguous parsing or accidental
collisions.

The outer component path also names each child pin, private node endpoint,
physical branch, mapping consumer, and compiled-diagram row. A child factory
may itself return a built composite, producing a longer path; built-ins and
custom components therefore participate in the same traversal.

Expansion is finite and acyclic. A snapshot may contain already-built nested
snapshots, but cannot contain itself through any descendant. The builder rejects
a cycle before returning its `ComponentInstance`; Julia walks the sealed tree
depth-first and stops only at primitive component snapshots. V1 defines no
numeric nesting-depth limit or truncating fallback.

## Seal the complete public and private graph

The snapshot records the following exact data before Plan sealing:

| Surface | Frozen content |
|---|---|
| Child hierarchy | Each child `component_path`, catalog/factory schema identity, ordered pin schema, public parameters, and either primitive leaf data or a nested snapshot. |
| Private topology | Every private node, its complete endpoint set of `(component_path, pin)`, and every unexposed child endpoint. |
| Canonical ground | The complete set of grounded endpoints; each local `ground()` group is retained in the diagram projection with its endpoint-derived identity. |
| Public maps | Explicit maps from public pin ID to one private node, public coordinate ID to one private node, public parameter ID to its `ParameterSpec`/baseline/binding consumers, and public inductive-branch ID to one oriented expanded branch. Public parameters retain the factory declaration order; map-like surfaces remain canonically sorted. |
| Binding graph | Each child physical slot is a constant, public-parameter identity, or declarative `AffineMap`; every repeated consumer remains a separate fan-out edge. |

No child pin, node, coordinate, parameter, or inductive branch becomes public by
name coincidence. A public pin is usable only for parent wiring; a public
coordinate is usable only for analysis selection; the same node appears in both
maps only when the factory exposed both roles. Hidden nodes and child parameters
remain snapshot evidence and cannot be selected by a parent or Runtime Spec.

The canonical physical snapshot, including all private children, paths,
endpoints, public maps, baselines, and bindings, contributes to the Plan hash.
The complete local ground-group list is preserved for authoring/compiled
diagrams but excluded from that physical hash: its grouping cannot change the
canonical ground or compiled operator. This matches the existing Plan identity
boundary in [Plan Sealing and Canonical Identity](plan-sealing-and-identity.qmd#separate-three-identities).

## Bind parameters as data

`ParameterSpec` and each public baseline are frozen at `build()`. Parameter
binding later resolves each child slot through exactly one of three data forms:

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| constant | A fixed physical value owned by that child slot. |
| identity | One exact public `ParameterRef`; repeated use is intentional fan-out. |
| `AffineMap` | `output = slope * input + intercept`, with the declared input ref and support evidence. |

The snapshot preserves every identity and map edge, including multiple child
slots fed by one `ParameterRef` and several different `AffineMap` outputs fed
by that same ref. It does not turn equal-valued constants into a shared
parameter or merge distinct maps. Julia evaluates these frozen bindings after a
`ParameterSet` is selected; it receives no Python callable, source object, or
AST. Invalid dimensionality, support, or mapped physical value follows the
existing typed failure path and never silently reuses a baseline.

The parameter meaning and calibration limits remain the public
[Parameter variants and derived mutual inductance](../component-authoring.qmd#parameter-variants-and-derived-mutual-inductance)
contract. This page adds no optimizer bounds, support tolerance, or acceptance
Gate.

## Expand one snapshot for both backends

Julia receives the sealed Plan snapshot plus the resolved physical parameter
binding. It validates snapshot structure and recursively emits one
backend-neutral physical graph in deterministic component-path order. Direct
and HB then lower that same graph; custom composites do not receive a separate
backend or a second source of topology.

| Snapshot content | Direct expansion | HB expansion |
|---|---|---|
| R/L/C child | One oriented linear physical branch | Corresponding linear row |
| JJ | `L_J0` at zero phase/zero bias and separately declared parallel `Cj` | Nonlinear Josephson row and the same separate `Cj` |
| Finite-loop SQUID | Two zero-phase/zero-bias `L_J0` junction branches, finite loop branch, and mutuals | Two nonlinear junction rows, finite loop branch, and the same mutuals |
| Mutual coupling | Signed branch orientations and derived `M` in the complete inductance system | The corresponding oriented solver coupling realization |

`josephson_inductance` is always the per-junction `L_J0`; it is not an inferred
finite-bias inductance. `junction_capacitance` remains an independent parallel
branch. A symmetric SQUID's two junction paths share the public parameter
identities while its loop branch retains its own orientation. The physical
meaning is unchanged from [Josephson Current, Phase, Energy, and Inductance](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/josephson-physics/josephson-current-phase-energy-and-inductance.qmd#independent-parallel-junction-capacitance)
and [DC SQUID Flux Tunability](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/josephson-physics/dc-squid-flux-tunability.qmd#finite-loop-mutually-pumped-dc-squid).

For every coupling, Julia binds the two oriented branch paths, resolves
`M = k * sqrt(L1 * L2)`, and validates the existing signed `k` and complete
reciprocal positive-definite inductance requirements. It neither guesses a
sign from drawing placement nor accepts an independent `M`. The physical
orientation and energy semantics remain canonical in
[Inductive Coupling Coefficient, Mutual Inductance, and Self Inductance](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/quantum-circuits/inductive-coupling-coefficient-mutual-self-inductance.qmd).

An exact declared zero may omit a backend row only after its component path,
declared value, and `omitted-as-zero` status are retained in the expanded graph
and evidence. Zero is therefore a documented physical declaration, not a
missing child, a dropped mutual, or a reason to collapse the remaining graph.

## Project the same snapshot two ways

The authoring diagram projects the semantic outer components, their public pins
and coordinates, actual outer wiring, and canonical ground. It preserves local
ground groups as glyph grouping while never creating more than one electrical
ground. It does not turn hidden children into public handles or show backend
rows.

The compiled diagram recursively projects the entire baseline snapshot. It
labels each expanded leaf and private node by its segment-array component path,
shows all ground groups and their mapping to canonical ground, preserves
parameter identity/fan-out, and marks every omitted zero term. It does not
perform PTC, coordinate transforms, Schur elimination, or Direct/HB numerical
analysis. Those request-specific facts remain with `run.explain()` and the
resulting typed evidence.

Both diagram forms are read-only projections of the same frozen graph. A theme,
layout, or local ground glyph cannot mutate the snapshot or rename Plan
identity. The public projection rules remain in
[Inspection and evidence](../component-authoring.qmd#inspection-and-evidence).

## Fail before a backend sees ambiguous topology

Python rejects incomplete public maps, foreign or duplicate child snapshots,
ambiguous component paths, cyclic nesting, incomplete nodes, invalid ground
endpoints, invalid map bindings, or an exposed reference that does not belong to
the composite. Julia rejects a snapshot whose canonical bytes, child provenance,
paths, parameter bindings, branch orientation, or recursive expansion do not
match the sealed Plan. Neither side imports a custom factory during execution,
fills a missing mapping by name, drops an ambiguous term, or substitutes a
primitive approximation.

Structural failure is distinct from a candidate-specific mapped nonphysical
value: the former prevents the Plan/request from reaching backend execution;
the latter follows the established candidate failure evidence. Neither creates
a new Human numerical threshold or an alternate successful model.
